documents.title: Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet V1.0: PETG HF
Bambu PETG HF Safety Data Sheet SDS20250724G02
Bambu Lab Filament Hex Code Table: PETG HF
Filament guide: printer, nozzle, AMS, build plate and glue compatibility

notes: Mechanical keys hold the TDS X-Y printed-specimen values; the registry has one key per scope, so the Z values (tensile 23 ± 4 MPa, elongation 5.1 ± 0.8 %, bending modulus 1810 ± 140 MPa, bending strength 48 ± 4 MPa, impact 10.6 ± 1.2 kJ/m²) are not stored. Density, melting, glass transition, Vicat and HDT are raw-material properties (ISO 1183, DSC, ISO 306, ISO 75) and sit under material.* / thermal.*, apart from the printed-specimen mechanical.* rows. The registry has no *.printed / *.material key pair, so the split is by key group and test_condition.

TDS facts with no registry key are not stored: Young's modulus (X-Y 1810 ± 190 MPa, Z 1540 ± 130 MPa), melt index (28.2 ± 2.7 g/10 min at 210 °C, 2.16 kg), crystallization temperature (N/A), heat deflection temperature 69 °C at 0.45 MPa, saturated water absorption rate (0.40% at 25 °C, 55% RH), printing and storage humidity (< 20% RH, sealed, with desiccant), nozzle size (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 mm; kept as a relation), bed surface preparation (glue), retraction length (0.8 - 1.4 mm) and speed (30 - 60 mm/s), chamber temperature (35 - 50 °C), max overhang angle (~ 70°), max bridging length (~ 30 mm), spool material (ABS, temperature resistance 70 °C) and spool size (diameter 200 mm, height 67 mm), annealing of prints (not recommended; if done, 75 to 80 °C for 4 to 8 hours), odor, skin hazards, chemical stability, solubility, chemical resistance, flammability and combustion products rows.
The TDS recommended chamber temperature (35 - 50 °C) is not written to thermal.chamber_temp: that key is a printer capability, not a filament print setting.

material.spool_type is not written: the store page has no spool bullet for this product (its Spool group offers "Refill" and "Filament with spool"), and the TDS gives the spool material (ABS) and size, not a spool type name. It is not marked not_published either, since the TDS does describe the spool.

SDS facts with no registry key are not stored: product name "Bambu PETG HF", model "G02-xx (xx stands for any suffix)", identified use "3D printing filament", CLP "Not classified", no hazard pictogram or signal word, no PBT/vPvB substance or endocrine disruptor, and "Not hazardous goods" for sea (IMDG), DOT, road (ADR/RID) and air (ICAO-TI) transport; SVHC "Not listed". Its section 9 "No data available" for melting point and density does not override the TDS values. Its section 5 says "No data available" for combustion products, while the TDS says "Water, carbon oxides".

Source differences kept for review (no conflict with the store page): bed temperature (TDS 65 - 75 °C vs material-table wiki 60 - 80 ℃); AMS drying (material-table wiki 65 ℃ for 12 h in the AMS 2 Pro and AMS HT, PETG wiki 65 °C, 8 h for AMS HT / AMS 2 Pro); heated-bed drying (TDS X1 Series 75 - 85 °C, 12 h; PETG wiki 80 °C, 12 h; drying wiki generic PETG row 75-85 ℃, 12 h). The product TDS values are kept for the spec keys. The nozzle temperature (230 - 260 °C) agrees between the TDS and the material-table wiki.

Drying requirement (no key): the material-table wiki says drying before use is "Required" and desiccant protection during use is "Required" for PETG HF / PETG Translucent; the store page says "PETG HF must be dried before use" and to keep it moisture-free during prints over 6 hours.

Build plate guidance: the TDS lists glue as the bed surface preparation and the material-table wiki recommends glue stick or liquid glue; this is a recommendation, not a stated requirement, so no requires relation is written. The Bambu Cool Plate / PLA Plate is "Not recommended" (material-table wiki), not "not compatible", while the store FAQ says "Compatible with all printers, AMS, build plate, and nozzles."; no relation is written for the Cool Plate.

The PETG wiki's "Printing suggestions for un-dried PETG HF" (Generic PETG HF parameters: nozzle temperature 220 ℃, volume speed 16 mm³/s) are a workaround for damp filament, not a manufacturer spec of this product: not stored.

Marketing prose proves no number: "Twice as fast as standard PETG", "superior resistance to water, UV, and temperatures", "Tougher and more durable than PLA" and "Smooth, Soft Texture" are not stored as values.
Hex: all 14 store colours have exactly one tile in the official table, matched by the colour name without the code in parentheses.

The store page links a "Filament RoHS" certificate (https://store.bblcdn.com/8171d8bdd1ef402bb81196229fc40eaa.pdf) that was not cached and not read, so safety.certifications is neither curated nor marked not_published.
The store page also links the wiki page https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/general/swaping-new-filament-with-bambu-reusable-spool, which was not cached and not read.
material.diameter_tolerance (± 0.03 mm) is the store page's own row (Product Features › bullet 5); the TDS gives no tolerance, so it is not restated here and not marked not_published.
No in-the-box list: no official packing list exists for this filament (the store page has no What's in the Box section).
The store FAQ (4.Safety Tips) and the PETG wiki say the filament is not food-grade / not food-contact grade; no registry key holds this.
